main_body: Timber-framed house: a large terracotta tile roof (rows 0-43) over a plaster and timber front wall (rows 44-94) with windows, a door and a hanging sign
top_band: Terracotta tile roof slope, rows 0-43 at x=48, made of tile courses in orange tones (L 104-188) with dark course-shadow rows between them; it ends at a lit eave edge at about row 42-43
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened slope seen from above, as in the Beodeul house references. It is clearly separated from the wall below by the eave edge and a shadow row under the overhang. The front wall is a vertical face with its own shading and timber framing. The windows have shutters and sills, and the door has a dark frame and lintel. No receding side faces are drawn. Both major parts, roof and wall, satisfy the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile highlights and dark course shadows, and the plaster has speckle. The windows and door are well detailed, with a median of 15 colours per tile. Two measured facts point to a shallower piece: only 47 distinct colours against 66 and 185 in the references, and 73% of dark edge pixels are neutral against 7-9% in the references. The silhouette is wrapped in a near-black, colourless line, which is the sticker look. Beodeul instead uses tinted dark-brown or red-brown outlines. Because of the neutral outline and the lower colour variety, it would look flatter than the references beside them.
